references.text: Abraham falls on his face (וַיִּפֹּל אַבְרָהָם עַל־פָּנָיו) when God speaks about Isaac, a direct parallel within the same chapter.
Moses and Aaron fall on their faces in response to God's presence, just as Abram did.
Joshua falls on his face to the ground and worships upon meeting the commander of the Lord's army, a parallel to falling down in humility before God's presence.
Ezekiel falls on his face when he sees the appearance of the Lord's glory, a strong parallel to Abram's reaction to God's revelation.
The disciples fall on their faces in fear during the transfiguration on the mountain, an act of reverence before divine revelation.
John falls as dead at Jesus' feet when he sees the glorified Christ, a parallel to falling on one's face upon encountering the divine.
Both verses illustrate the same response to divine revelation: total submission and awe by falling on one's face.
The servant's reaction mirrors Abraham's own response in 17:3: total submission and worship at God's revelation.
Both verses describe God's revelation to Abraham; 17:3 is a deeper development of the covenant content that was introduced in 12:7.
